I kept seeing the same story from indie game devs. They ship a patch on Steam and a week later they find out from Valve's review or from a Steam Deck player that the game no longer starts under Proton.

Nobody did anything wrong. They just don't own a Deck and Valve only reviews the build after you submit it. By then the bad patch is already out.

So I built Protonaut. It's a GitHub Action that runs your Windows game build under Proton on every pull request, on a normal GitHub runner. If a change breaks the game on Linux, the PR goes red before it ever reaches players.

GitHub: Mahan-Imanian/protonaut · Demo PR: protonaut-demo/pull/1

The problems it catches

These are the ways a Windows game breaks under Proton that you'd normally only hear about from players:

  • The game crashes on start. Protonaut catches the crash and pulls the exact line out of Wine's log, like wine: Unhandled division by zero at address ..., so you don't have to dig through thousands of lines.
  • It runs, but the screen is black. Every run is captured, and black or empty frames are flagged.
  • It shows an error instead of the game. OpenTTD, run without its graphics files, keeps going while it displays "Missing graphics: OpenTTD requires graphics to function" inside its own window. A crash check would call that a pass. Protonaut reads the game window and flags error text like that.
  • An extra window or dialog pops up, like an "unsupported hardware" box, a launcher or a fatal error dialog.
  • The build itself has a problem: a DLL the game imports that nothing provides, files that only differ by letter case, or anti-cheat and launcher files worth a closer look.

What you get on the pull request

This is the comment Protonaut left on a build that crashes on start:

You get the failed checks, the crash line, screenshots and logs as an artifact, and a single command that reproduces the run on your own Ubuntu machine. See it live on the demo pull request.

Setup

It's one step after your build, on ubuntu-24.04:

- uses: Mahan-Imanian/protonaut@v0
  with:
    build: dist/Windows
    exe: MyGame.exe

The step fails the PR on any failure, writes the report to the job summary, and uploads the screenshots and logs. If you're on Godot, Unity or Unreal, there are ready-made workflows to copy in the recipes.

How it runs without a Deck or a GPU

A GitHub runner has no screen and no GPU, so Protonaut brings its own:

  1. A virtual display. It starts a headless display at 1280x800, the Deck's resolution.
  2. Rendering on the CPU. It draws with Mesa's software Vulkan driver, so any runner works.
  3. A pinned GE-Proton. Your build runs under a GE-Proton release checked against its SHA-256 before use.
  4. A sandbox. The game runs as a separate user, with no network and no access to your CI secrets.

Proven on real games every week

CI runs real open-source games through the action every week:

  • OpenTTD 15.3 (OpenGL)
  • Godot's 3D platformer demo, exported for both Vulkan and Direct3D 12
  • Chocolate Doom 3.0.1 with Freedoom (32-bit)

Every result with screenshots is in real-games.md.

Try it

If you ship a Windows game on Steam, add the step to your workflow and open a pull request. You'll know in a few minutes whether your build still runs under Proton.

It's open source, written in Rust under Apache-2.0. If it catches something or misses something, tell me in the comments or open an issue.

What's broken on Proton that you only found out about from players?

Protonaut is an independent project, not affiliated with Valve.
